scope: Flow-based detector for volumetric and scanning behavior. Not a general NIDS. Botnet, web attacks, infiltration, zero-day, and blocking are out of scope.

provenance.id_note: The id column restarts at 1 in the official test set and is a row index, not a stable flow key. It is excluded from the feature hash and must not be used for grouping or leakage detection.
provenance.source_note: Local download. Record the official source URL, citation, and licence before publication.
provenance.licence_status: not recorded; verify the official terms and citation before publication

provenance.source_note: Local download of the per-day CIC-IDS-2018 CSVs. Record the official source URL, citation, and licence before publication.

coverage_gate.reason: Required families are absent from the dataset: PortScan. Families absent from at least one partition: DDoS, DoS. Validation and test positive families do not overlap.

coverage_gate.reason: Required families are absent from the dataset: PortScan.

decision.unsw_nb15_verdict: usable for a leakage-safe, random-split coverage study, but not as a direct external validation of the CIC-trained model because 4 Tier A features are missing
decision.cic_ids_2018_verdict: contains DoS and DDoS across several days but no PortScan at all. A day-based split fails the coverage gate because the positives are concentrated in the early days; a group-hash split can cover DoS and DDoS only. It cannot close A4 for a claim that includes PortScan.
decision.reason: No dataset currently provides a validated, schema-compatible split that covers every required family in train, validation, and test. The audit records feasibility; it does not authorize a fit.

notes: No model is trained, no registry row is written, and the serving artifact is untouched.
UNSW-NB15 has no timestamp, so its split is a deterministic group-hash split, not a temporal split.
UNSW-NB15 duplicate groups are keyed on the 42 non-metadata feature columns.
CIC-IDS-2018 is a day-scheduled dataset. The audit reports a temporal day split and a group-hash split separately; only the group split can cover DoS and DDoS in all partitions.
CIC-IDS-2018 has no PortScan family, so any claim that includes PortScan remains blocked on data.
CIC-IDS-2018 duplicates are grouped on flow features after dropping direct identifiers (Flow ID, Src IP, Src Port, Dst IP).
The audit reads local downloads only; source URLs and licences must be recorded separately.
findings: UNSW-NB15: the official split is 175,341 train / 82,332 test. The local filenames match the official split.
UNSW-NB15: DoS (volumetric) and Reconnaissance (scanning) are the only in-scope positive families. Both appear in all three proposed partitions, so the coverage gate is PASS.

UNSW-NB15: feature-identical rows are pervasive. The audit removed 45,545 duplicate train rows, 20,152 duplicate test rows, and 953 test rows that duplicated a train group. It also excluded 1,772 train groups (30,528 rows) and 575 test groups (8,809 rows) whose feature-identical rows had inconsistent labels. A random split without this grouping would leak near-identical flows.

UNSW-NB15: only 8/12 Tier A features are available. 4 are missing (packet_length_max and the three flag counts). The CIC-trained serving model cannot be applied directly; a UNSW-specific model or a new feature adapter would be required.

CIC-IDS-2018: the complete local set contains 10 capture day(s) (2018-02-14, 2018-02-15, 2018-02-16, 2018-02-20, 2018-02-21, 2018-02-22, 2018-02-23, 2018-02-28, 2018-03-01, 2018-03-02) and 12,079,420 unique feature-identical flows after removing 3,931,926 within-file and 221,597 cross-file duplicate rows. Observed volumetric families are DDoS, DoS; required families missing from the whole set: PortScan.

CIC-IDS-2018: the day-based temporal split FAILS the coverage gate. All DoS and DDoS positives fall in the early capture days, so a 60/20/20 day split leaves validation and test with no volumetric positives. A day split is therefore a family split.

CIC-IDS-2018: a deterministic group-hash split FAILS the coverage gate. It can place DoS and DDoS in all three partitions, but it cannot manufacture a PortScan family that the dataset does not contain, and it is a random split, not a temporal one.

CIC-IDS-2018: all 12 Tier A features are present under CICFlowMeter-2018 names, and the 84-column 02-20 export reduces to the same 80-column schema after dropping `Flow ID`, `Src IP`, `Src Port`, and `Dst IP`.

CIC-IDS-2018: data-quality warnings remain. 59 repeated header rows were removed; 14 rows carry pre-2000 (mostly 1970) timestamps; 7 files have exactly 1,048,575 rows, consistent with a 1,000,000-row cap above the header. The 4 GB 02-20 file is not capped and is the only 7.9M-row day.
